name: Discipulus Ventures
identity_check: Confirmed as Discipulus Ventures (discipulusventures.com; LinkedIn company page and X account linked from the site), the El Segundo, California (Los Angeles area) firm led by General Partner Jakob Diepenbrock that runs a two-week in-person founder cohort for early-stage hard-tech and defense founders, investing $175,000 on acceptance. The site's own press list links the Axios Fund II story (June 2026) and TechCrunch's March 2024 launch article, and Deseret News and the LA Business Journal describe the same El Segundo accelerator and founder. Founders' testimonials call it 'DV'. Not Disciple Media or any other similarly named firm; the lead's 'LA' location is El Segundo, a separate city next to LAX.

thesis_text.value: Pre-seed firm that runs a two-week, live-in residency in El Segundo for about ten value-driven founders per cohort, building hard tech and software for Western interests: defense, energy, mining, manufacturing and other critical industries. It argues top talent is diverted from national priorities and explicitly backs founders motivated by religion, patriotism and family rather than wealth.

open_items: Fund I size, legal name and close date not found on any fetched page. The firm's site and iConnections say only that the first fund is '4x'; Deseret News (Apr 2026) says 'the company’s funds total $40 million', which with the $30M Fund II implies roughly $10M, but that is an inference. Search-result hints of a '$9M inaugural fund' and a Forbes (Feb 2025) '$6 million' raise are unverified: Forbes returned 403.

Fund II: size and description come from the press list on discipulusventures.com; the Axios exclusive itself (2026-06-29) returned 403, so close date is the Axios publication date and LPs (search snippets name Palmer Luckey and Brian Armstrong) are unverified and not recorded.

Only 5 portfolio rounds naming Discipulus were found (target 8). Western Chemicals, Titan Dynamics and Hedges rest on database pages only (CB Insights, Caplight, Signalbase); Aleph Surgical on Dealroom News plus InforCapital; Actinide on the company's own release. Not recorded because the fetched round page does not name Discipulus: Durin $3.4M pre-seed (TechCrunch 2025-04-23), Poseidon Aerospace $11M seed (2025-11-05) and $60M Series A (2026-09-08), Vanguard Defense $5M seed (Pulse 2.0 / VCA, 2026-03-25; Caplight lists $6.3M without Discipulus), Rune Technologies seed and Series A (Caplight investor table), General Galactic and Rainmaker (search results only).

Featured cohort companies with no round page found: Framework, Watoga, 1AU Technologies, Tex, Anew Technology (iConnections: Discipulus 'in at $2.5M', company 'now raised $30M round'; no round page), plus Lark Aeronautics and Athanor (PitchBook search hint, June 2026 seed; PitchBook returned 403).
portfolio_count_reported not stated by the firm. Deseret: fourth cohort in Apr 2026 and '10-20 new companies to El Segundo a year'; the cohort page lists 13 featured investments.
HQ: the firm's own pages place it in El Segundo, CA; a search snippet says PitchBook lists Mill Creek, Washington (not fetched, 403).
Leads: no evidence of Discipulus leading any round; VCSheet says 'Can They Lead? No'. Stated stage is pre-seed, but Caplight shows it in seed rounds (Actinide, Titan Dynamics).

requires_us_entity: unknown. The cohort FAQ welcomes international applicants and does not require an incorporated company to apply, but says nothing about the entity needed for the $175,000 investment. Nothing found on Indian founders.

TechCrunch (Mar 2024) named Isaac Yi (COO) and William Pan (EIR) as co-founders; neither appears on the current team page, so they are not recorded. CFO Kristina Dayback and the five Senior Advisors (Josh Manchester, Kevin Hartz, Ben Kohlmann, Josh Steinman, Isaiah Taylor) are on the team page but not recorded as partners.
Application form is a third-party miniextensions.com link from the site's 'Apply' buttons; contact is a partner's email address (not recorded).
